zea-plant.name: Teosinte
zea-plant.summary: The wild grass species native to Mesoamerica from which maize (Zea mays) was domesticated, belonging to the same genus, Zea.

three-sisters-agriculture.name: Three Sisters
three-sisters-agriculture.summary: A companion-planting method combining maize, beans and squash, in which each crop supports the others, developed by Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

archaic-period-in-mesoamerica.name: Archaic period (Mesoamerica)
archaic-period-in-mesoamerica.summary: A period in Mesoamerican history from about 8000 to 2000 BCE, marked by crop domestication, the rise of agriculture and the beginning of settled life.

guil-naquitz-cave.name: Guilá Naquitz Cave
guil-naquitz-cave.summary: A cave in Oaxaca, Mexico, site of the earliest known domestication of squash on the continent and among the earliest evidence of maize domestication.

oaxaca.name: Oaxaca
oaxaca.summary: One of Mexico's 31 states, in the south of the country, known for its Indigenous peoples, especially the Zapotecs and Mixtecs, and archaeological sites such as Monte Albán.

balsas-river.name: Balsas River
balsas-river.summary: A major river of south-central Mexico flowing through Guerrero, México, Morelos and Puebla into the Pacific Ocean; rapids limit navigation, so it is used mainly for hydroelectric power, flood control and irrigation.

ortoiroid-people.name: Ortoiroid people
ortoiroid-people.summary: Second wave of settlers of the Caribbean, who began migrating into the Antilles around 2000 BC, apparently from the Orinoco valley. Their name comes from Ortoire, a shell midden site in Trinidad.

zohapilco.name: Zohapilco
zohapilco.summary: An archaeological site in central Mexico dating from 5500 to 2200 BC, known for the earliest ceramics found there and links to the Tlatilco and Olmec cultures.

olmecs.name: Olmecs
olmecs.summary: An early Mesoamerican civilization that flourished roughly 1200 to 400 BC in what is now Veracruz and Tabasco, known for colossal stone heads and considered one of the cradles of civilization.

richard-macneish.name: Richard MacNeish
richard-macneish.summary: American archaeologist (1918–2001), nicknamed "Scotty", whose fieldwork transformed understanding of how agriculture developed in the New World. He also pioneered new fieldwork methods and interdisciplinary collaboration.

coxcatlan-cave.name: Coxcatlan Cave
coxcatlan-cave.summary: Archaeological site in the Tehuacán Valley, Puebla, Mexico, discovered by Richard MacNeish in the 1960s. Its early domesticated plants changed how the timing of plant domestication in Mexico was understood.

banwari-trace.name: Banwari Trace
banwari-trace.summary: Pre-ceramic Archaic site in southwestern Trinidad, the oldest archaeological site in the Caribbean. It shows two periods of occupation, between 7200 and 5500 years before present.
